🇲🇽🎨 <u>Zócalo's Giant Catrina: 1.6 Million Visitors in Four Days</u>

Mexico City's Monumental Catrina, more than 33 meters tall and recognized by Guinness, drew 1.6 million visitors to the Zócalo in four days. Tourism, food and Day of the Dead festivities brought in more than 15 billion pesos. Add Formula 1, and the city's total reached 36 billion. By popular demand, she stays until November 11.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Heads to COP31: "Mexico Is Back"</u>

Mexico arrives at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey (November 9–20) with ground to make up: in 2025 it generated a quarter of its electricity from low-carbon sources, only 13% from renewables, and 74% from fossil fuels. The 2025–2030 plan to strengthen and expand the national grid would add 22,000 MW. "One of the important messages to the COP is that Mexico is back," Adrián Fernández of the Iniciativa Climática de México told IPS.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The INE's Favorite Suppliers Came From the CISEN</u>

José Alfredo and Raymundo Hernández Casillas, the brothers behind the ballot-supply network now under investigation, started at Gobernación in 1983 and moved to the CISEN, the PRI-era political intelligence agency, in 1989 under Salinas. Anti-Corruption Secretary Raquel Buenrostro laid out the trail: their front companies won more than 2 billion pesos in contracts from 23 of the 32 state electoral bodies between 2014 and 2023, without owning the machinery to make electoral materials. Their old boss at the CISEN, Juan Carlos Padilla Aguilar, now sits in the leadership of the right-wing party Somos, the same party as Lorenzo Córdova.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Topolobampo: Ammonia Plant Machinery Heads Back to the US</u>

Heavy equipment for Proman-GPO's planned ammonia plant at Topolobampo, Sinaloa, is being pulled out. Supplier Fagioli's temporary import permits are expiring, and the machinery has to be back in the US by November 15. The company insists the project isn't cancelled. The Mayo-Yoreme "¡Aquí No!" collective, camped outside for more than 150 days, calls it a win and vows to keep fighting for Ohuira Bay, a Ramsar-listed wetland.

🇲🇽💧 <u>Mexico's "Water Millionaires": 1.1% of Users Hold 22.3% of the Water</u>

An Ibero study of Mexico's public water-rights registry (REPDA) found that 3,304 users (966 companies, 1,537 individuals and 800 civil associations) hold 22.3% of all water concessioned in the country. That's 1.1% of all users. In 2020, 115 of Mexico's 653 aquifers were overexploited, and the "water millionaires" were drawing from 99 of them. This is the map that Salinas' 1992 National Water Law drew when it turned water into concessions.

🇲🇽🌎 "We have a very good relationship with China, and a very good relationship also with the government of the United States." "We decided to raise some of the tariffs on China in December of last year, but out of a decision of our own, of Plan México." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Plan Michoacán report, Nov 4, 2026 US Ambassador Ronald Johnson said China would be happy to see a chaotic US-Mexico border. China's embassy replied that Washington is trying to sow discord between Mexico and China. Asked about it, Sheinbaum said Mexico's main trade partnership is North America and it has no free trade agreement with China. She noted that US automakers in Mexico themselves import many parts from China. The only country Mexico has no relations with, she said, is Ecuador, "for having invaded Mexico's embassy." "We don't want this to be a debate in Mexico."

🔥🇲🇽 "What moral authority does Ugalde have to talk about democracy? None." "He was the articulator, the executor of the electoral fraud orchestrated by Vicente Fox himself and Calderón." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Plan Michoacán report, Nov 4, 2026 Former IFE president Luis Carlos Ugalde called for a review of all past electoral contracts and a "consensus" pick for the new INE head. Sheinbaum pointed to his own book, where he says he was named by the PRI on Elba Esther Gordillo's recommendation, and to Fox's admission days earlier that he made Calderón win in 2006. She added that Lorenzo Córdova, as INE president, did nothing about the two companies that have won the contracts for electoral materials for more than 20 years.
